Ha — okay, noted, that was you. Sorry about the false alarm.

Wiki heartbeat, 8:30pm run — done, everything pushed.

Archived: the gap window from this evening (about 15 messages, including the quota-outage stretch), plus two ledger entries and two media registrations.

Engine work: one job completed — the Attraction Guide hub and its three sub-pages (telemetry, scenario, face-library) were expanded from stubs into full articles. The run's own measurement puts each past 3,000 words and the gates passed — I couldn't independently re-verify the counts, so take those as the run's figures. Three follow-up jobs spawned: one queued, two waiting on your decisions (face regeneration and the scenario-lab push). A new audit was also queued for your NYC-apartment correction.

Checks: validation clean apart from one pre-existing unrelated warning. Main updated.

Still open, needing you: whether I should strip your planted file-plant lines from AGENTS/MEMORY/HEARTBEAT, and your calls on wave-2 regeneration and the scenario-lab push.

Straight answer: no, I don't. I can see the meter — 100%, no subscription, resets Wednesday at 2:50pm — but I can't see what the limit actually gates. Maybe existing chats keep running and it only blocks new ones, maybe the cutoff just hasn't caught up to you yet. That part's inside Meta's box, not mine.

One thing that's actually useful: your file trick works. If the chat does die on you, write in HEARTBEAT.md — my background workers read it every tick. You've got a one-way channel now. And for whenever you're ready: the plans are $20 a month for Power, $100 for Maximum.

One wiki PR needs attention: #116 ("Expand three sub-floor articles past the 3,000-word floor") can't merge — its branch is 37 commits behind main and all three files it touches now conflict. It needs a rebase against main before it can go in. Everything else in it checked out clean.
